content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Vulnerability Assessment and Scanning with Nessus and OpenVAS"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Vulnerability assessment is a critical component of ethical hacking and proactive cybersecurity. It involves systematically identifying, quantifying, and prioritizing vulnerabilities in computer systems, applications, and network infrastructures. This tutorial covers two of the industry-standard vulnerability scanners: Nessus and OpenVAS."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Vulnerability Scanning"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before running scans, it is essential to understand the difference between active and passive scanning, authenticated versus unauthenticated assessments, and how scanners use vulnerability databases (such as CVE and CVSS) to rate risks."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Active Scanning: Directly probing target systems to identify open ports, services, and known vulnerabilities."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Authenticated Scanning: Providing credentials to the scanner to inspect internal configurations, missing patches, and local files."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Unauthenticated Scanning: Black-box approach simulating an external attacker without internal access."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Nessus: Setup and Basic Scanning"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Nessus by Tenable is a widely adopted proprietary vulnerability scanner. After installation, it is typically accessed via a web interface running on port 8834."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"sudo systemctl start nessusd"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once started, navigate to https://localhost:8834 in your browser. To perform a basic network scan, configure a new scan policy:"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Select 'Advanced Scan' or 'Basic Network Scan'."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enter the target IP address or subnet CIDR notation (e.g., 192.168.1.0/24)."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure credentials under the 'Credentials' tab if performing an authenticated assessment."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"3. OpenVAS (Greenbone Vulnerability Management): Open-Source Alternative"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"OpenVAS is a fully featured vulnerability scanner maintained by Greenbone Networks. It utilizes a regularly updated feed of Network Vulnerability Tests (NVTs)."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"sudo gvm-start"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"After starting the GVM services, access the Greenbone Security Assistant (GSA) web interface. To execute a scan using the command line or interface, ensure your feeds are synchronized."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"sudo greenbone-nvt-sync"},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Analyzing Results and Remediation"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Both Nessus and OpenVAS categorize findings by severity levels: Critical, High, Medium, Low, and Info. Ethical hackers must analyze these results carefully to filter out false positives before presenting the report to stakeholders."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Verify critical findings manually using tools like Metasploit or Nmap scripts."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Prioritize remediation based on CVSS scores and exploitability."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Generate executive and technical reports for compliance and mitigation tracking."}]
